record_links.rationale: This record introduces the compass activity that leads to constructing a 60 degree angle.

record.evidence_quote: Here is a fun activity for you to do: Use a compass and draw a circle. Keep the position of the legs of the compass the same for the whole activity. Make a dot anywhere on the circumference of the circle. Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss
record.content_text:
Here is a fun activity for you to do: Use a compass and draw a circle. Keep the position of the legs of the compass the same for the whole activity.

Make a dot anywhere on the circumference of the circle.

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-062.png

Put the compass on the dot and start to make small arcs on the circumference of the circle:

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-063.png

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-064.png

You will find that you can fit in exactly six of these small arcs:

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-065.png

You know that a full turn (or revolution) is equal to $360^{\circ}$, so if we join the centre of the circle to each one of the six small arcs, we form six angles of $60^{\circ}$ each.

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-066.png

If you are asked to construct an angle of $60^{\circ}$, you simply do a part of the fun activity that you have done above.

record_links.rationale: This worked example gives the straightedge-and-compass procedure for constructing a 60 degree angle.

heading_path.h3: Worked example 14.5: Constructing an angle of 60 degrees

record.evidence_quote: You are given a line segment $BD$ as shown below. Construct $AB$ so that $C$ is a point on $AB$ and $A\hat{B}C = 60^{\circ}$. Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-067.png
record.prompt_text:
You are given a line segment $BD$ as shown below. Construct $AB$ so that $C$ is a point on $AB$ and $A\hat{B}C = 60^{\circ}$.

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-067.png
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Draw the first big arc.

Put the compass point at point $B$ and draw a big arc. Label point $C$ where the arc crosses line segment $BD$. Keep the compass at the same width for Step 2.

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-068.png

Step 2: Draw a small arc that crosses the first big arc.

Keep the compass at the same width as for Step 1. Put the compass point at point $C$ and make an arc to cross the big arc that you drew in Step 1.

Label the point of intersection $A$.

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-069.png

Step 3: Complete the construction.

Use a ruler and draw a line segment from point $B$ through point $A$.

Source image reference: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-14-070.png

Step 4: Check your work.

Use a protractor to measure $A\hat{B}C$. The angle should be equal to $60^{\circ}$.

record_links.rationale: This note explains why the 60 degree construction is equivalent to constructing part of an equilateral triangle.

record.evidence_quote: When you construct an angle of $60^{\circ}$ you are actually constructing a triangle with three equal sides. In an equilateral triangle all three sides have equal lengths and each of the angles are equal to $60^{\circ}$.
record.content_text: When you construct an angle of $60^{\circ}$ you are actually constructing a triangle with three equal sides. In an equilateral triangle all three sides have equal lengths and each of the angles are equal to $60^{\circ}$.
